Poppy-fields.notes: Read from src/Poppy-Fields.cpp at commit 71e0bcb, the last commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.30. Four places where the code and Manual-Poppy_Fields.md disagree. The Smooth inputs run the opposite way from the Smooth knobs: the knob value is subtracted from 1 (line 688) while the input is used as it stands (line 690), so 0V at the jack gives the most slew where a knob at 0 gives none; the manual says only that the inputs replace the knobs. The length and Start inputs are truncated with int() before being scaled (lines 569 and 574), so only whole volts count and only six values can be reached, which the manual does not mention. Zoom shrinks the drawn window as 2 divided by the square of the setting (lines 635 and 636), which at the maximum of 15 is about 225 times rather than the 50 the manual names. The manual says the Petals input adds a small offset along with the absolute value; line 585 adds no offset. The Mutagens knobs are configured from -1.8 to 1.8 (lines 279 and 280) but the value is clamped to ±1.5 (lines 592 and 593), so the ends of their travel do nothing. The panel-theme submenu is plugin-wide and cosmetic, so it has no line.

The fourth Constants knob is configured as Throw (line 137) while the panel and the input name print Hold, so its hover text differs from the panel. The EDIT - conditions button has no printed label at all; while it is latched on, generateOutput takes the branch at line 423 and writes no output voltages, so the outputs freeze. The manual says the Influence knobs at full put Spawn midway between its parents; the code adds one hundredth of the gap per step (lines 386 and 387), which is a pull rather than a position. The maker's Haste description calls the knob volt-per-octave tuned; it scales a modulation rate, not a pitch, so the jack is marked cv. Simone-Chaos.notes: Read from src/Simone.cpp at commit 71e0bcb, the last commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.30. Three things the manual does not say. Drive is not a drive: LydFilter.h:162 crossfades a lowpass and a highpass of the same signal, and Simone.cpp:399 uses the knob as that crossfade position, so the knob moves the output from lowpass to highpass with no non-linearity anywhere. The Wave knob also sets that filter's corner, at 220 times two to the power of the Wave value (Simone.cpp:401). The Gain attenuverter offsets the Gain knob when nothing is patched, because Simone.cpp:393 substitutes 1 for an unconnected jack rather than 0, so the attenuverter's setting is added to the knob directly. The big knob is configured as Speed while the panel prints Pitch, and the range button is configured as Range while the panel prints Speed, so both hover texts differ from the panel. Ledger-Logic.notes: Read from src/Ledger.cpp at commit 71e0bcb, the last commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.30. Three places where the README and the code disagree. The README says a block becomes independent once both its inputs are connected; Ledger.cpp:272 tests only the second input, so patching the first input alone leaves the block cascading. The README says an unconnected first input is normalled to NOT the first input of the block above; Ledger.cpp:264 normals it to that block's first flip-flop, which is not the same thing and is not brought out to any jack. The README describes the second input as normalled to the same operation's result from the block above; Ledger.cpp:265 normals it to the previous block's second flip-flop. Canyon-Echo.notes: Read from src/Canyon.cpp at commit 71e0bcb, the last commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.30. The buffer is 352800 samples (Canyon.cpp:14), which the maker's comment calls about eight seconds; the delay block is stepped every second sample, so the entry states the time as a fraction of the buffer rather than in seconds. Feedback is multiplied by 1.1 before the jack is applied and clamped at 1.1 (Canyon.cpp:342 and 344), so the top of the knob is above unity gain and the lines build rather than decay; nothing on the panel says so. In Light/Dark the filter corner is worked out from the unclamped knob-plus-jack sum and only the crossfade position is clamped (Canyon.cpp:357 to 359), so a large CV can push the corner far outside the 300Hz to 1200Hz the knob alone reaches. The Feedback, Freeze and Reverse controls are marked with glyphs rather than words, as are their jacks, and the four small CV attenuverters have no labels at all. The module has no right-click menu of its own, so no panel-colour choice. There is no manual and no README entry for it.

Seethe-Distort.notes: Read from src/Seethe.cpp at commit 71e0bcb, the last commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.30. Every Mix knob defaults to 0, which is fully dry, so a new instance passes its input through without any saturation until one of them is turned up; nothing on the panel says so. The Curve controls are doubled up: Seethe.cpp:274 uses the value as the tension of the waveshaper and Seethe.cpp:275 uses the same value to set the band's filter frequency, two octaves either side of 450Hz, 850Hz and 1500Hz, so the crossover moves with the tone. The three curves the Morph knob crossfades are built at Seethe.cpp:198 to 200 as a symmetrical sigmoid, a full-wave rectified sigmoid and a sine fold; a half-wave curve is written in the file but never used. Each band output is high-passed at 15.2Hz to take out the offset the rectifying curves create. The module has no right-click menu of its own, so no panel-colour choice, and there is no manual or README entry for it.
